answer: Temporal Nectar Echo Windows. Each identity must emit a nectar pulse at a randomized offset within its assigned window, then an echo reply after a fixed propagation delay; late or early pulses are rejected. The window schedule derives from a quartz-seeded clock shared across nodes, so offsets cannot be precomputed. An attacker running N fake identities must maintain N simultaneous live pulse-echo loops with correct timing, paying per-identity compute and bandwidth for continuous clock sync.
